thread:
AJ: Heads-up: customer X pressing for a hard 99p latency commitment for chat-gen. Need to align SLOs, rollout, and fallback UX by COB Tues.
Maria: We're not hitting that now. Last perf run shows 99p ~ 560ms for hosted under typical traffic. 400ms is unrealistic for hosted without tradeoffs.
Dianne: Suggest tiered commitments: hosted standard, dedicated premium SLA. That gives sales something to sign with.
Samir: Yes. Also we need clear automatic fallback in the spec: if 99p > threshold for window, switch to smaller model or trim context. Define exact trigger windows.
AJ: Acceptance criteria to include in PRD: measurable baseline, canary plan, rollback criteria, public degrade messaging. We should spell out customer-visible behavior.
Maria: Draft acceptance criteria proposal:
- Hosted default: 99p <= 600ms for 7 consecutive days on baseline workload
- Dedicated SLA: 99p <= 400ms with reserved capacity
- System error rate < 0.5% (5xx + timeouts)
- Canary: 10% traffic, 24h, no regressions on latency or errors
- Automated fallback triggers documented and tested
Samir: Edge cases to call out: cold-starts (KV cache misses), bursty eval traffic, cross-region failovers, cache warm-up after deploys. Also document amplification when clients retry.
Leo: UX for graceful degrade: return structured flag so callers can surface a soft notice instead of error. Example payload snippet: 
```
{ "text": "...", "degraded": true, "degraded_reason": "context trimmed to 512 tokens" }
```
Maria: Ops questions we need answered in PRD: who owns alerts for canary regressions? what's error-budget burn policy — auto-throttle or manual intervention?
Dianne: Ops (oncall-eng) will own canary alerts. Error-budget policy: automated throttling of concurrency for offending route, page PM + SE on high burn. Document escalation path.
AJ: Rollout plan (add to PRD):
1) full internal perf run + 48h synthetic soak
2) 10% canary for 24h with full observability
3) 50% ramp over 48h monitoring latency and errors
4) GA and SLA enforcement
Samir: Include a compatibility matrix mapping model variants -> fallback variants (quantized -> fp16 fallback, smaller context variants) and latency expectations per variant.
Maria: Also list acceptance test harnesses: perf harness, chaos (inject KV misses / higher latency), canary anomaly detectors, and example customer contract language for degrade scenarios.
AJ: I'll update the PRD draft and link it here. If no major objections, we'll freeze SLOs for launch next Tuesday. :thumbsup:
OpsBot: Reminder: add oncall rotation for canary watches to the rollout checklist.
Dianne: I'll add fallback pseudocode to RFC and the rollout checklist items.
Samir: Also propose a short customer-facing FAQ blurb describing what "degraded" looks like and expected retry behavior.
Maria: Good call. I'll loop in Sales and CSM to get customer commitments and confirm enterprise wording.
AJ: Thanks all — please keep comments inline on the PRD draft. We need acceptance criteria and rollback playbook in place before we start canary.
